sentences.text: Hydrotherosaurus was a medium-sized plesiosaur estimated to be 7.8 to 8.8 meters long and weigh around 1.9 metric tons.
It possesses one of the longest necks relative to body length among elasmosaurids, containing 60 vertebrae in total.
The animal had a small head about 33 cm long, an aerodynamic body, and four large flippers specially designed to help the animal balance, move, and accelerate.
In 1943, Samuel Paul Welles identified the specimen as distinct enough to describe as a new genus and species, naming it Hydrotherosaurus alexandrae.
The specimen was displayed at the Golden Gate International Exposition and the University of California Berkeley before being stored in the 1960s.
Hydrotherosaurus is classified within the family Elasmosauridae.
The animal lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
